t: You are looking at numbers fifteen to twenty-seven Pelham Crescent, a curved terrace in Kensington and Chelsea. It was designed by George Basevi, a pupil of Sir John Soane who worked in both Neoclassical and Gothic Revival styles. Basevi also designed Belgrave Square in London and the Fitzwilliam Museum in Cambridge. He was surveyor to the Thurloe estate, which is the connection to this part of London.
